evidence.quote: Optimizing the mechanical properties of dual-phase Ti-6242s titanium alloy at 550 °C using the boundary architecture

In this work, a comparative investigation is performed to examine the mechanical properties of Ti-6242s alloys at 550 /C14 C with two representative microstructures, i.e., the equiaxed and semi-equiaxed microstructures.

evidence.section: 3.3. Microstructural evolution during tensile tests at high temperature
evidence.quote: Therefore, for the S0 sample composed of an equiaxed microstructure, the softening behavior is ascribed to dynamic recovery and recrystallization of the a phase during tensile testing at 550 /C14 C[ 21,29,34].
The nano-scale b phases act as an obstacle to increase the resistance to dislocation movements and limit dislocation multiplication in the ap.

In the case of limited slip transfer from the ap to btrans, a substantial pile-up of dislocations occurs at the ap/btrans boundary during deformation at high temperature, causing high strain localization in the equiaxed microstructure.
This high strain localization promotes recrystallization in the a phase and eventually causes a decreased strength at high temperature.

(2) Dynamic recrystallization occurred in the a phase adjacent to the ap/btrans boundaries, where strain concentration occurs under tension and mainly accounts for the decreased strength in the equiaxed S0 sample.
These nano-scale plates/precipitates of the b phase lying in the ap effectively impede dislocation slips and enhance the deformation resistance of the ap phase.
slip is limited by the b nanoplates in the ap, increasing the deformation resistance.

however, the ap/btrans boundary is displaced by a transition region in the semi-equiaxed microstructure. Such a transition region redistributes the local strain effectively and alleviates the strain localization during the deformation process.
A homogeneous strain distribution is achieved, and recrystallization of the a phase is inhibited in the semi-equiaxed structure. Therefore, the strength at high temperature is signiﬁcantly increased.
